summary.headline: The Trails Committee refined its $466,628 Community Preservation Act application for the Peninsula Trail footbridge ahead of Fall Town Meeting.
summary.summary: The Trails Committee finalized details on its request for $466,628 in Community Preservation Act funding to construct the Peninsula Trail footbridge for the October Town Meeting warrant. Members discussed conducting public outreach through a Southborough Access Media video and hosting an informational booth and guided trail walk during Heritage Day weekend. The committee also reviewed a pending $4,739 Choate Fund grant for trail enhancements and discussed the environmental suitability of pressure-treated lumber for local boardwalks and bog bridges.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from July 16, 2026, as amended. Routine scheduling and adjournment were also completed.
key_details: Minutes from July 16, 2026 approved.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase II CPA grant application
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the final draft of its Community Preservation Act application for the Peninsula Trail footbridge project before the September 15 deadline. The total project cost of $466,628 requests $210,796 in new CPA funding, combined with repurposing $211,232 and $44,600 from previous Town Meeting appropriations. The committee discussed Community Preservation Committee feedback regarding bridge construction estimates derived from a 65/35 split of previous bids, as well as plans to produce an informational video with Southborough Access Media.
key_details: Total CPA funding request is $466,628 for the pedestrian footbridge.
Includes $210,796 in new CPA funds and repurposing $255,832 in previously approved CPA funds.
Budget includes $345,440 for bridge construction, $34,800 for project management by Pare Corp, $12,500 for engineering support by VHB, and $68,888 in contingency.
Final application deadline is September 15 for the October Town Meeting warrant.
topics.outcome: Application finalized to submit to the Community Preservation Committee, with upcoming appearances planned before the Select Board and Advisory Committee.
topics.why_it_matters: The proposal asks Town Meeting voters to authorize $466,628 in town Community Preservation Act funds to construct a pedestrian bridge completing the Peninsula Trail.

topics.title: Choate Fund grant application
topics.summary: The chair summarized an application submitted to the Choate Fund for $4,739.77 to support accessibility and trail enhancements on the Peninsula Trail. The proposed work includes expanding gravel pads around four existing interpretive signs to accommodate benches and discourage weed encroachment, as well as installing an additional bench and a youth-oriented interpretive sign.
key_details: Grant application submitted for $4,739.77 from the Choate Fund.
Expands four existing gravel sign pads using J and J Sun Quote.
Adds one new youth-focused interpretive sign and an additional bench.
Grant award decisions expected from the Choate Fund by the end of August.

topics.title: Trail shed security and tool storage
topics.summary: The chair reported that replacement tools purchased for trail maintenance remain stored in her garage while security arrangements are made. The committee plans to coordinate with the Department of Public Works regarding security cameras before returning tools to the shed.
key_details: Tools remain secured offsite until shed security is installed.
Committee plans to coordinate with DPW on security camera options.
A committee work session will be scheduled to assemble new equipment.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; coordination with DPW pending.

topics.title: Heritage Day outreach and trail events
topics.summary: Members discussed participating in the upcoming Heritage Day celebration in October to inform residents about the Peninsula Trail project and the Town Meeting CPA warrant article. The committee also discussed coordinating with the Department of Conservation and Recreation to lead a guided history hike along the trail prior to Town Meeting.
key_details: Heritage Day takes place during the Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples Day weekend.
Committee plans to host a pop-up tent to share information on the CPA bridge proposal.
Committee plans to explore hosting a guided history walk with a DCR ranger.
topics.outcome: Members agreed to coordinate booth staffing and explore scheduling the history hike.

topics.title: Pressure-treated lumber review and trail access inquiry
topics.summary: Meeting participants reviewed recent research finding that modern copper-treated lumber (ACQ/MCA) has minimal environmental impact on surrounding soil, noting the Conservation Commission approved its use for an Eagle Scout bog bridge project at Kallander North. Participants also noted that neither the MWRA nor DCR restricts its use. Additionally, a resident inquiry regarding an eroded public path between Big Oak Woods and Wentworth and Heather Lane was discussed, noting the strip is town-owned property.
key_details: Research indicated copper migration from treated lumber is limited to within one inch of direct contact.
Conservation Commission approved treated lumber for an Eagle Scout project at Kallander North.
Trails Committee has stored lumber intended for bog bridges on the Peninsula Trail and Templeman trail.
Town-owned strip of land connecting Wentworth and Big Oak Woods will be reviewed with the Conservation Agent and DPW.
topics.outcome: Treated lumber confirmed acceptable for ongoing trail repairs; neighbor inquiry referred to town staff.

topics.title: Misdirected applicant redirection
topics.summary: Representatives for a property at 45 Southville Road mistakenly joined the Trails Committee meeting seeking approval for a porch demolition. The chair assisted the applicants by providing the correct Zoom link for the Conservation Commission meeting taking place concurrently.
key_details: Applicants sought a permit hearing for 45 Southville Road.
Chair emailed the Conservation Commission Zoom link and alerted the Conservation Agent.
topics.outcome: Applicants successfully redirected to the Conservation Commission meeting.

public_comment.summary: A resident and volunteer reported that the Conservation Commission approved the use of ACQ and MCA pressure-treated lumber for an Eagle Scout boardwalk project at Kallander North after reviewing studies showing minimal soil contamination. The resident also reported receiving an inquiry from a neighborhood resident about an eroded public connector trail between Wentworth Drive, Heather Lane, and Big Oak Woods.
